sections.title: A rare Fijian tree
sections.text: Syzygium phaeophyllum is a poorly known evergreen tree recorded from Taveuni, Fiji, in wet tropical forest. The original collection described a tree about 6 m tall with smooth bark and stiff, round brown twigs; it is known from very few historical collections.

sections.title: Leaves and evidence
sections.text: Its leathery elliptic leaves are about 6–8 × 2.5–4 cm, tapering near the base and pointed at the tip; flattened leaf stalks measure about 6–10 mm. Reliable species-specific details of its flowers, fruit and food uses were not found, so none are inferred from other Syzygium.

sections.title: Plate
sections.text: The foliage-only plate is appropriate: it shows the elliptic, leathery leaves and brown twig, while avoiding an unsupported flower or fruit depiction.
